## Research Trajectory

**Published context:** The identified source study reports spatial coarsening in this mechatronic metamaterial system. The supplied export is one 2,199-sample experimental aggregate, not 2,199 independent runs. The follow-up does not claim to rediscover coarsening or establish a new mechanism.

**Question and conditional hypothesis:** Does mean shear depend only on instantaneous correlation width, or does it also depend on the recent coarsening path? The proposal was that, at matched widths, shear might differ when width is growing versus shrinking. That would be consistent with lagged response or hysteresis, but could also reflect shared time trends, smoothing, or noise. The prediction was that lagged width change would improve held-out prediction and that a growth-versus-decline contrast would remain directionally stable after accounting for time and serial dependence. Neither outcome is proof of a mechanism.

**Observed data and analysis trajectory:** The supplied measurements had 2,199 rows, no missing required values or duplicate timestamps, and highly regular 0.003333-second spacing. Width ranged from 0 to 17.1456; shear ranged from 0.04599 to 0.21571. Their descriptive Pearson correlation was 0.5492. The first analysis reported a small lag-model improvement, but its matched-width contrast and bootstrap were judged invalid: the contrast pooled across time, and bootstrap indexing broke the intended contiguous resampling. A subsequent attempt failed because the time-only model requested a nonexistent feature column. After that was fixed, the lagged model performed slightly worse than the width-plus-time baseline. A later contrast and bootstrap were again judged mismatched to the intended estimand.

The final reported analysis used actual elapsed-time lag differences and recomputed the matched growth-versus-decline contrast in contiguous-block bootstrap replicates. Blocked expanding-window results were: time-only RMSE 0.01038949, MAE 0.007651518; width-plus-time RMSE 0.009663956, MAE 0.007268262; and the 0.10-second lag-augmented model RMSE 0.009677134, MAE 0.007350481. Lag sensitivities were worse at 0.05 seconds (RMSE 0.01053883, MAE 0.008081386) and substantially worse at 0.20 seconds (RMSE 0.02332396, MAE 0.01407957). The final matched-width support was 1.5746–13.4715, with 986 growing and 756 shrinking samples. The smoothed growth-minus-decline shear contrast was -0.003122128; its reported 95% block-bootstrap interval was -0.004902243 to 0.002571514, spanning zero.

**Interpretation and open alternatives:** These results do not support the proposed predictive-memory pattern in this export: the primary lag model did not improve on width plus time, and the final directional contrast was uncertain. Residual lag-1 autocorrelation remained high (0.8652), so substantial temporal structure was unmodeled. Expanding-window validation tests later periods and may confound prediction with regime changes. The bootstrap interval is descriptive for this single aggregate, not independent-run inference; its 30-sample blocks may not capture the dependence indicated by residual autocorrelation, and direction labels were not recomputed from each resampled trajectory. Accordingly, neither the score differences nor the contrast establish absence or presence of physical memory. Shared temporal trends, export aggregation or smoothing, measurement noise, and insufficiently representative block uncertainty remain alternatives. Repeated runs, raw image sequences, and documented uncertainty would be needed for stronger tests; novelty beyond the supplied source context remains unresolved.
